title: Dropping a style on words inside a copy says they are not text
goal: Drag a text style onto the label inside a copy of a component and the app refuses it with "Save button is not text". The thing under the pointer plainly is text. The rule that a copy answers as a whole is fine; the sentence explaining it is not, because it tells the person something they can see is false.
notes:
From the rough list of queue/audits/2026-09-09-text-style-drag.json: "Text inside a copy of a component reads as the copy rather than as text, so a style dropped on it is refused with is not text. That is the same rule every click on a copy follows, but the sentence is misleading there."

The sentence is Sources/PhotonzCore/TextStyleDrop.swift:93. The target resolution that makes a copy answer instead of its piece is Sources/Photonz/CanvasGroups.swift componentPiece, and Sources/PhotonzCore/ComponentInstances.swift.

This is a wording and honesty fix. Changing the RULE so a style can land on a piece inside a copy is a bigger question (it would be a sixth kind of override) and is not in scope; if the runner thinks it should be, file it as a follow-up with a card rather than building it.
acceptance: Aiming a text style at words inside a copy says what is really going on, in words that do not contradict what is on screen, and points at the way to do it if there is one
Aiming at something that genuinely is not text is unchanged
To see it: Scripts/probe-app.sh, place a copy of the starter Button component, save a text style, and drag its tile over the copy’s label
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) The lie is worse than it looks: a first-time user does not know the button is a copy, so 'Save button is not text' reads as the app being broken, and there is nothing on screen that hints at a way forward. (2) The rule itself is right and stays: a copy answers as a whole, the hit test stops at the copy (Document.hitTestPath), and a per-copy text style would be a sixth kind of override. Out of scope, per the task. (3) Shortest thing that delivers the value: name the piece and its original in the sentence the person is already reading, and point at the two moves that DO work (set the style on the original, or detach this copy). No new control, no new state. (4) Cut: no outline around the words on a refusal. The accent outline means 'this will take the style', and drawing one on a no would contradict the colour. (5) Honesty edge: for a copy inside a copy, detaching the inner copy does not stick (the outer sync rebuilds it), so the detach clause is dropped there rather than offered falsely.

Built and verified. Core: TextStyleDrop gains CopyPiece (the piece name, the original's name, and whether detaching is a real way forward), and PhotonzDocument.textStyleCopyPiece(at:) reaches one level past the copy the hit test stops at, only to SAY what is there. The canvas fills it in when a not-text hit turns out to be a copy. Nothing about what a drop DOES changed. Tests first: 6 new tests in TextStyleDropTests, whole suite 5344 tests green.

Second review, on the real app (Scripts/playtest/style-on-a-copy-walk.json, new). The pill reads 'Label comes from Button. Set Heading on the original, or detach this copy.' and sits below-right of the pointer, clear of the words it is about. It is the longest line this pill ever says but stays one line and legible in the capture. Left as is: no outline on a refusal (an accent ring means yes), and no pointer to WHERE detach lives (no room in one line). Walks: style-on-a-copy passes first time, text-style x3 pass, copy x9 pass.

Follow-ups filed. (1) 'A button grows when a style makes its words bigger' (p2, ui-layout): REPRODUCED by the new walk, the pill stays 78 px wide while its words go from 11 px to 32 px, renders 2-copy.png and 5-copy-follows.png. (2) 'Decide whether a style can be set on one copy without detaching it' (p2, ui-components), blocked on a decision card with a brief at queue/decisions/decide-whether-a-style-can-be-set-on-one-copy-wi-should-one-copy-of-a-component-b.md, so nobody builds the sixth kind of override before the user has answered. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-09-style-on-a-copy.json with two real window captures.

The refusal over a copy's words now reads 'Label comes from Button. Set Heading on the original, or detach this copy.' (PhotonzCore TextStyleDrop.CopyPiece + textStyleCopyPiece, wired in CanvasTextStyleDrop). Verified by 6 new core tests, the full suite (5344 green), and a new walk style-on-a-copy-walk.json that reads the sentence back and proves the way out; text-style and copy walks unchanged. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-09-style-on-a-copy.json with two real captures. Two follow-ups filed, one of them behind a decision card. Pushed as 982e6c64.
